title: Find the Unique Permission Code
real_world_story: A system stores permission or access-operation codes generated from multiple user requests. Every code appears exactly twice except one code that appears only once. The system needs to identify the unique code.

real_world_connection.target_represents: The code that appears only once
real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: Bitwise XOR, where identical values cancel each other and the unique value remains

problem_statement: Given an array of integers where every value appears exactly twice except one value that appears exactly once, find and print the value that appears only once.
task: Use XOR to identify the unique permission code without using extra storage for frequencies.
input_format: The first line contains an integer N. The second line contains N space-separated integers.
output_format: Print the integer that appears exactly once.
constraints: Every value appears exactly twice except one value that appears once

examples.explanation: The values 1 and 2 appear twice, while 4 appears only once.
The values 9, 7, and 3 occur twice, leaving 5 as the unique value.

expected_algorithm.name: Single Number
expected_algorithm.reason: XOR cancels equal pairs because x XOR x is 0, leaving the value that occurs only once.

hint: Initialize an XOR result to zero.
XOR the result with every value in the array.
Pairs of equal values cancel each other.
The remaining value is the unique permission code.
real_world_takeaway: XOR-based single-number detection can identify an unmatched access code efficiently without maintaining a frequency table.
